summary: A brutal economic engine-builder where you open burger, pizza, and sushi restaurants, hire and train staff, and blast the board with advertising to steer a fixed pool of customers to your tables. Turn order is earned rather than given, so a strong early lead compounds into a runaway win while late movers can be locked out entirely.
praised: no rubber-banding — good decisions actually snowball
huge variety of viable opening strategies
satisfying "aha" moment when an engine clicks
criticised: brutal to new players, especially in a 4-5p game
very long teach and long playtime
can feel solved/mathematical rather than thematic
a bad early game can be unwinnable by turn 3

interaction.kind: direct competition for a shared customer pool and blocking
interaction.detail: All players sell into the same finite demand track, so opening a restaurant or advertisement directly reduces what's available to everyone else, and recipe/discount choices are explicitly aimed at undercutting opponents. Employee hiring and firing timing lets you deny cheap staff to rivals, so most of the tension is about denying resources rather than sharing a board.

scoring.why: Whoever ends the game with the most cash wins, and cash comes almost entirely from restaurant sales minus wages and setup costs.
scoring.how_you_win: You build a machine of restaurants, staff, and marketing that serves more customers more profitably than anyone else, then hold onto that lead to the final count.
